summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with altered mental status, fever, and hyperkalemia after missing a dialysis session. He had a history of dialysis line infections and seizure disorder. Initial workup revealed a potassium of 6.8, treated with insulin, glucose, and kayexalate, followed by hemodialysis. Blood cultures grew beta strep group C and coagulase-negative staph, prompting IV vancomycin for suspected line-related bacteremia. A CT head showed no acute findings. The patient refused a lumbar puncture. His mental status improved, and he remained stable after dialysis. Despite recommendations to complete IV antibiotics inpatient, he chose to leave against medical advice on hospital day two. Arrangements were made for IV antibiotics during outpatient dialysis. He was counseled on medication adherence, particularly for seizure prevention.
